newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Romanian cargo ship adrift off S.Africa east coast.
newsitem.headline: Romanian cargo ship adrift off S.Africa east coast.

text.p: A Romanian cargo ship with 22 people on board has gone adrift in heavy seas off South Africa's east coast, officials said on Friday.
The Liberian-registered 4,800 dwt Calarasi, owned by the Navrom company of Constanza, was drifting about 10 miles off Port St Johns.
"We received a mayday signal at about 9 a.m. today from the Calarasi saying she had engine problems and that she needed assistance," said an official of the National Sea Rescue Institute.
A South African Air Force plane had been sent from Durban to search for the vessel.
"All ships in the area have been notified and a tug has been sent from East London harbour to assist," Durban port spokeswoman Yvonne de Kock said.
The ship's destination and point of departure were unknown, as was its cargo.
Two South African Air Force helicopters carried out the rescue.
"The helicopters sighted 12 people in a dinghy about 20 miles off Port St Johns," Captain Joy Rautenbach told Reuters. "It looks like the ship has gone down."
She said the survivors were being brought ashore while the search continued for the rest of the crew.

The 4,800 dwt Calarasi lost power due to engine problems and began drifting. A distress signal was received at 0700 GMT by South Africa's National Sea Rescue Institute and a tug from the port of East London was sent to the area.
